issues.title: Ballykissangel
issues.notes: Year range (1996–2001) is correct. US BritBox is confirmed. However, Reelgood (updated June 2026) reports the show is 'not currently available to stream, rent, or buy in the UK,' casting doubt on the UK BritBox claim. No Australian-specific BritBox listing was found either; JustWatch AU data for BritBox did not surface this title. The UK and AU BritBox listings are unverified and likely inaccurate.

issues.title: Downton Abbey
issues.notes: Year range (2010–2015) is correct per Wikipedia and IMDB. US: Peacock confirmed; Netflix US is NOT available (Downton Abbey is not in the US Netflix library). UK: ITVX confirmed; Netflix UK is confirmed. AU: Binge confirmed; Foxtel confirmed; but Netflix AU is not confirmed (TechRadar and JustWatch AU list Binge/Foxtel/BritBox/Prime Video, not Netflix AU for the TV series). The guide incorrectly lists Netflix for the US region and is uncertain for Netflix in AU.

issues.title: Cranford
issues.notes: Year range (2007–2009) is correct. US BritBox is confirmed. However, 'PBS Masterpiece' is not confirmed as a current standalone streaming platform for this title — JustWatch US lists BritBox, Peacock Premium, and Hulu but does not list a separate PBS Masterpiece channel for Cranford. 'PBS Masterpiece' is now largely integrated into Peacock, not a distinct streaming destination. UK BritBox and AU BritBox could not be independently confirmed from search results. Status flagged as issue due to the PBS Masterpiece listing being outdated/inaccurate as a current streaming platform.

issues.title: Foyle's War
issues.notes: Year range (2002–2015) is correct. US Acorn TV confirmed. UK: ITVX is confirmed (free and premium), and Acorn TV UK is confirmed. AU Acorn TV is confirmed. However, the UK listing should also note Netflix UK, Sky Go, and Now TV are available per JustWatch UK — but those are not listed in the guide, which isn't necessarily wrong. The main issue is that JustWatch UK also shows Netflix as a UK streaming option, which the guide omits. The guide's listed platforms are confirmed as present but the UK claim of 'Acorn TV' as a distinct UK streaming service is confirmed.

issues.title: Hamish Macbeth
issues.notes: Year range (1995–1997) is correct. US BritBox is confirmed (all three seasons added January 2026). The guide lists 'Buy on Amazon' for the US as a secondary option, but JustWatch and Moviefone show it is now fully streamable on BritBox and also on Acorn TV, Prime Video, Tubi, and Pluto TV — 'Buy on Amazon' is no longer necessary as a primary listing and is an outdated characterisation. UK BritBox and AU BritBox could not be independently verified from search results.

issues.title: Rosemary & Thyme
issues.notes: Year range (2003–2007) is correct. US BritBox is confirmed. However, Acorn TV is NOT confirmed for the US — Reelgood (updated June 2026) lists BritBox, Prime Video, Hallmark+, Tubi, and others but does NOT list Acorn TV for the US. UK: ITVX is confirmed (free and premium); BritBox UK is not confirmed in search results. AU: Acorn TV AU could not be confirmed — no Australian-specific Acorn TV listing was found for this title.

issues.title: The Vicar of Dibley
issues.notes: The year range (1994–2020) is correct — the main series ran 1994–2007 but lockdown specials aired in December 2020, per Wikipedia and IMDB. US BritBox is confirmed. UK: BritBox UK is NOT confirmed — a dedicated BritBox UK tracking site (newonbritbox.info) states 'The Vicar of Dibley is no longer available to stream on BritBox in the UK.' AU: BritBox AU and Stan are confirmed per Apple TV AU listings. 7plus could not be independently confirmed.

issues.title: McDonald & Dodds
issues.notes: The guide lists this as '2020–present' but the show was cancelled after four series on 16 January 2025; it is no longer ongoing. The year range should be 2020–2024. Streaming platforms are confirmed: US BritBox confirmed, UK ITVX confirmed, AU BritBox confirmed per Collider and Wikipedia.

issues.title: George Gently (Inspector George Gently)
issues.notes: Year range (2007–2017) is correct. US Acorn TV is confirmed. AU Acorn TV is confirmed. UK: BBC iPlayer is NOT confirmed as a current full streaming home — a Grokipedia episode list (as of October 2025) notes 'BBC iPlayer offers limited episodic availability…but not comprehensive catch-up for the full run.' JustWatch UK lists Netflix, Sky Go, Now TV, and Amazon Prime Video for the UK — not BBC iPlayer or BritBox. Both UK platforms listed in the guide appear inaccurate.

issues.title: Hetty Wainthropp Investigates
issues.notes: Year range (1996–1998) is correct per IMDB (listed as 1995–1998 on IMDB; first episode aired January 1996 per JustWatch). US BritBox is confirmed; 'Buy on Amazon' is outdated — the show is now fully streamable on BritBox and no longer primarily a purchase-only option. UK: JustWatch UK lists Sky Go, ITVX, BritBox, Now TV — BritBox UK appears confirmed. AU BritBox could not be independently verified.

issues.title: Harry Wild (Season 5) — Acorn TV arrival: New episodes weekly · Finale July 27
issues.notes: Season 5 premiered on June 22, 2026, not in July. The finale date of July 27 is confirmed correct, and episodes do drop weekly, but the guide omits the already-aired June 22 premiere date and presents Harry Wild as a new July arrival when it actually began in June.

issues.title: Murdoch Mysteries (Season 19) — Acorn TV arrival: New episodes weekly
issues.notes: Season 19 premiered on Acorn TV on March 2, 2026, not in July. By July 2026 it is in its final weeks (finale episode airing July 20 in the US), so listing it as a July arrival is misleading — it is a carryover, not a new arrival.

issues.title: You're Killing Me (Series 1) — Acorn TV arrival: New episodes weekly
issues.notes: The series premiered on May 18, 2026, and its six-episode run concluded with its finale on June 22, 2026 — well before July. The full season is already available on Acorn TV; listing it as a current 'new episodes weekly' July arrival is inaccurate.

issues.title: Gone (Series 1) — BritBox highlight: BritBox Original · North America Premiere · July 23
issues.notes: The July 23 North America premiere date is confirmed. However, 'Gone' is not a BritBox Original — it is an ITV/All3Media production that BritBox acquired the North American rights to. Multiple sources identify it as a BritBox exclusive/North America premiere, not a BritBox Original.

issues.title: A Woman of Substance (Series 1) — BritBox arrival: New episodes Wednesdays · Finale August 5
issues.notes: The Wednesday cadence and August 5 finale are confirmed correct. However, the series premiered on BritBox on June 24, 2026 (not in July), so listing it as a July arrival is inaccurate — it is a carryover continuing into July with weekly Wednesday episodes.

issues.title: Vera
issues.notes: Year range (2011–2025) is correct. US streaming on BritBox and BritBox via Amazon is confirmed. UK streaming on ITVX is confirmed. However, AU streaming is listed as 'BritBox, Foxtel / Binge' — sources confirm BritBox is the primary AU streamer for all 14 seasons, and while Foxtel carries some seasons, no evidence was found that Binge (a separate Foxtel-owned service) currently carries Vera. The AU listing may be partially inaccurate by including Binge explicitly, and omitting that Foxtel is confirmed. Additionally, UK listing omits that BritBox UK was absorbed into ITVX Premium in April 2024 and no longer exists as a standalone UK platform.

issues.title: Midsomer Murders
issues.notes: The show is ongoing (1997–present) so year range is fine. US: Acorn TV is confirmed as the primary US streamer (with exclusive new seasons); BritBox Amazon Channel is also listed on JustWatch, so both US platforms are plausible. UK: ITVX is confirmed; however, BritBox UK ceased to exist as a standalone platform in April 2024 and was absorbed into ITVX Premium — the guide should not list 'BritBox' as a separate UK platform. AU: Acorn TV and BritBox AU — JustWatch AU does not prominently list BritBox as a current AU streamer for Midsomer Murders, and Acorn TV holds exclusive new season rights in the US/Canada but AU rights are unclear; this listing is uncertain.

issues.title: Happy Valley
issues.notes: Year range (2014–2023) is correct. US: The guide lists 'AMC+ / Acorn TV' — AMC+ and Acorn TV were correct for season 3 in 2023, but as of August 2025, BritBox has acquired all three seasons for the US. JustWatch US now lists BritBox (not AMC+) as the primary subscription streamer. The US listing is outdated. UK: BBC iPlayer is confirmed; Netflix is listed, but Happy Valley was removed from Netflix UK in March 2020 — it is NOT currently on Netflix UK; BBC iPlayer is the correct UK platform. AU: BritBox and Stan are both confirmed AU streamers.

issues.title: Inspector Morse
issues.notes: Year range (1987–2000) is correct. US: BritBox only — confirmed by JustWatch US. UK: The guide lists 'ITVX, BritBox' — ITVX is confirmed; however, BritBox UK ceased to exist as a standalone platform in April 2024 (absorbed into ITVX Premium tier). It should not be listed as a separate UK platform alongside ITVX. AU: BritBox AU is confirmed (some seasons via Flicks). The UK dual-listing of ITVX and BritBox as separate services is inaccurate post-April 2024.

issues.title: Endeavour
issues.notes: Year range (2012–2023) is correct. US: PBS Masterpiece is confirmed; BritBox is listed but JustWatch US currently shows PBS/PBS Masterpiece as the primary streamer — BritBox does not prominently appear as a current US home for Endeavour on JustWatch. UK: ITVX is confirmed; BritBox UK is listed but it ceased to exist as a standalone UK platform in April 2024 (absorbed into ITVX Premium). AU: BritBox AU is confirmed; Foxtel/Binge also carry it per Flicks.com.au, but the guide only lists BritBox which is the main platform.

issues.title: Lewis
issues.notes: Year range (2006–2015) is correct. US: JustWatch US lists BritBox as a current streamer; PBS Masterpiece is also cited in older sources for season 9 — plausible but uncertain if both are currently active. UK: ITVX is confirmed (ITV.com hosts Lewis); BritBox UK is listed separately but ceased to exist as a standalone UK platform in April 2024 (absorbed into ITVX Premium). AU: BritBox AU is not prominently confirmed on current AU JustWatch listings; the show appears on Flicks as available to buy but not clearly on BritBox AU subscription.

issues.title: Broadchurch
issues.notes: Year range (2013–2017) is correct. US: Netflix returned to US on November 1, 2025 (confirmed); Peacock is confirmed; PBS Masterpiece is confirmed — so all three US platforms check out. UK: The guide lists 'Netflix, Buy on Amazon / Apple' — Netflix UK did add Broadchurch in November 2025 (confirmed); however ITVX also streams it and is not mentioned. The listing is incomplete for UK (missing ITVX) but Netflix UK is now accurate. AU: BritBox AU is confirmed; '10 play' (free) is also confirmed on JustWatch AU and Flicks — so AU listing checks out. The main issue is the UK listing omitting ITVX.

issues.title: Line of Duty
issues.notes: Year range (2012–2021) is now outdated — Series 7 was confirmed by the BBC on 18 November 2025 and is in production, so the end date of '2021' is no longer accurate; it should be listed as '2012–present' or '2012–'. US: BritBox is confirmed as the exclusive US home for series 6 and future series; Hulu held early seasons but is not a current confirmed streamer — the guide's inclusion of Hulu is outdated. UK: BBC iPlayer is confirmed; Netflix UK re-added all six series on 27 June 2025, so Netflix UK is now accurate. AU: The guide lists 'BritBox, Netflix' — AU JustWatch lists Stan (not Netflix) and BritBox/Foxtel/Binge; Netflix AU does not appear to currently carry it. The AU Netflix claim is incorrect; Stan is the correct AU platform.

issues.title: Shetland
issues.notes: Year range (2013–present) is correct (Series 10 aired in late 2025, Series 11 commissioned). US: BritBox only — confirmed by JustWatch US. UK: BBC iPlayer is confirmed; BritBox UK is listed separately but ceased to exist as a standalone UK platform in April 2024 (absorbed into ITVX Premium). Additionally, the show is on BBC iPlayer (and Sky Go), not BritBox UK as a separate entity. AU: BritBox AU is confirmed as the primary streamer for all seasons.

issues.title: Death in Paradise
issues.notes: Year range (2011–present) is correct (Season 15 aired in early 2026, show renewed through at least 2028). US: BritBox only — confirmed as the US home for all seasons. UK: BBC iPlayer is confirmed; BritBox UK is listed separately, but BritBox UK ceased to exist as a standalone platform in April 2024 (absorbed into ITVX Premium). It should not be listed as a separate UK platform. AU: BritBox AU is confirmed; however, sources also indicate Binge carries it in Australia (per WhatToWatch and JustWatch AU), so listing only BritBox AU is incomplete.

issues.title: You're Killing Me (Series 1) — Acorn TV arrival, full season now streaming
issues.notes: The series premiered May 18, 2026 with weekly episodes, and the 6-episode season finale aired June 22, 2026. As of July 20, the full season is indeed now streaming, so the 'full season now streaming' claim is accurate for today's date. However, the guide implies it is a current highlight rather than a completed run — the show finished its weekly rollout on June 22.

issues.title: Gone (Series 1) — BritBox highlight & arrival, BritBox Exclusive, North America Premiere, July 23
issues.notes: The July 23 North America premiere date and 'BritBox Exclusive' label are confirmed by multiple official sources. However, the guide labels it only as 'BritBox Exclusive,' omitting that it is also officially designated a 'BritBox Original' in all official BritBox press materials. The distinction matters: it was produced for ITV in the UK first, airing in February 2026, so the 'Original' designation is specifically for North America. The 'Exclusive' label alone is not wrong but is incomplete.

issues.title: Grace (Season 6) — BritBox arrival, July 2
issues.notes: Grace Season 6 premiered on ITV in the UK on March 29, 2026. Multiple sources confirm it will not arrive on BritBox in the US until early 2027, following the typical ~11-month delay for this non-BritBox-Original series. No credible source places it on BritBox in July 2026. The Wikipedia entry for Grace notes that Season 5 arrived on BritBox from July 2, 2024 — the July 2 date in the guide likely refers to Season 5, not Season 6.

issues.name: And Then There Were None
issues.notes: The description says the strangers are 'lured to an island', which is broadly accurate, but more precisely they are 'invited' (not all were lured in the same way). More significantly, the description says they are 'murdered one by one', which is accurate in spirit. However, the plot summary omits that they are accused of past crimes before being killed — a key plot point. The number 'ten' is correct. This is a minor framing issue rather than a clear factual error, so 'confirmed' could also apply; however the word 'lured' is a slight inaccuracy — in the source material they are 'invited', not universally lured.
issues.title: And Then There Were None

issues.name: The ABC Murders
issues.notes: John Malkovich does star as Poirot, but the description calls him 'aging' — in the show Poirot is depicted as older and somewhat forgotten, so that is fair. More importantly, the serial killer works through the alphabet by location and victim name initials, not literally 'through the alphabet' in a simple sense, but this is a reasonable shorthand. The claim is broadly accurate. However, a factual note: the show aired on BBC (not ITV), which the fan site may be implying is an ITV production given the page context. No explicit network error is stated in the claim itself, so no issue there. The description is essentially confirmed.
issues.title: The ABC Murders

issues.name: Ordeal by Innocence
issues.notes: The description says 'a wrongful conviction is called into question', but in the show (and novel) the convicted man (Jack Argyll) has already died in prison — an alibi emerges posthumously, meaning the conviction is proved wrongful after the fact. The central drama is that someone else in the family must be the real murderer. The phrase 'wrongful conviction is called into question' is imprecise and slightly misleading: the conviction is not merely 'called into question' — it is established as wrongful, redirecting suspicion to the family. A more accurate description would note that a posthumous alibi proves the convicted man innocent, throwing the family into turmoil.
issues.title: Ordeal by Innocence

issues.name: The Pale Horse
issues.notes: The description says 'a dealer in antiquities is drawn into a web of witchcraft and murder.' In the 2020 BBC adaptation, the lead character Mark Easterbrook is described as a 'widowed antique dealer' (or in the TV version an antiquities-linked character), so the 'dealer in antiquities' detail is partially correct. However, the witchcraft element is accurate. The more significant issue: in the original novel the protagonist is not primarily a 'dealer in antiquities' — he is a historian/writer. In the BBC TV adaptation, Zachariah Osborne (played by Bertie Carvel) is actually the enigmatic antique dealer, while the protagonist Mark Easterbrook is the one drawn into the mystery. The description misattributes the 'dealer in antiquities' role to the protagonist.
issues.title: The Pale Horse

issues.name: The Seven Dials Mystery
issues.notes: The description says 'a string of alarm clocks and a murder', but in both the novel and adaptations there is specifically one set of eight alarm clocks (placed as a prank), not 'a string' of separate incidents. Additionally, the most recent major TV adaptation (Netflix, January 2026, titled 'Agatha Christie's Seven Dials') is not a BBC or ITV production. The original 1981 LWT adaptation is the main British TV version. The claim of 'a string of alarm clocks' slightly misrepresents the singular prank involving eight clocks. The description is otherwise recognisable but imprecise.
issues.title: The Seven Dials Mystery
